summary: Tested the SIV relay that runs from the driver's device while the server-side Adif connection was forced to fail with a simulated 403. Before the relay, GET /api/trains returned source=null and alerts=[] for both stations, as expected. After logging in (admin/admin) and opening Trenes, the browser opened wss://info.adif.es/InfoStation and POSTed /api/trains/siv-snapshot for 60000 and then 17000 (200 each, within ~4s), then fetched /api/trains again. siv-info-atocha/chamartin were shown. Atocha had 2 alerts ('Convocatoria de huelga en Ouigo' and 'Circulación interrumpida en la línea de alta velocidad Madrid-Andalucía', which expands to show the full text). Chamartín had 1 alert. siv-source-* read 'Fuente: paneles de la estación de Adif · HH:MM'. A curl afterwards gave source='siv', real data_time, alerts present, and operators Renfe/Iryo/Ouigo at both stations. Reopening the tab while the server copy was fresh sent no POST. When only one station was stale, only that station was posted (17000). Historical time-range queries sent only GETs with start/end_time and no relay; this is a real check because historical responses always have source=null and would count as stale without the isHistorical guard. When the relayed copy was older than 4 minutes, the next tab load relayed again and recovered on its own. Backend tests: 8 new tests in test_siv_relay.py, all pass (401 without auth, 400 for an invalid station, 422 for a missing payload, 413 for more than 400 trains, accepted:false for missing, invalid or stale (>5 min) data_time, and a duplicate post accepted then rejected). The cercanías-only alert filter works. Together with test_trains_siv_api.py: 14 passed, 1 skipped.

minor.issue: Found in code review, not run against the server. A data_time in the future passes the freshness check because (now - dt) is negative, so it is never more than 300. The snapshot is then stored as _last, and every real relay with an earlier data_time is rejected until that future time passes. One device with a wrong clock, or one malicious authenticated user, can freeze station data and alerts for hours. Fix: reject a dt more than about 60s after the current time.

SIV info (alerts, cancelled count, data_time) is kept only in process memory. After any backend restart or reload, GET /api/trains returns source=null and alerts=[] until a driver opens the Trenes tab again. This was seen during testing: hot-reload at 22:13:05 wiped Chamartín's SIV info. If production runs several uvicorn workers, a relay received by one worker is invisible to GETs served by another. Consider saving the latest parsed snapshot per station in Mongo.

Trust model: any logged-in user can post arbitrary alerts and arrivals, and they are shown to everyone. There is no per-user rate limit and no sanity check on the payload. Acceptable for an MVP, but worth a rate limit and logging.

integration_issues.issue: Opening the tab sends GET /api/trains?shift=all twice at the same moment (fetchData runs twice). The relay is not duplicated because of the inFlight guard, but the second GET is wasted.

action_items: Reject relayed snapshots whose data_time is more than about 60s after the current time (adif_siv.ingest_relayed_payload)
Optional: save the latest SIV parse per station in Mongo so alerts and source survive restarts and multiple workers
Optional: remove the duplicate GET /api/trains when the Trenes tab is opened
Remember to revert the simulated 403 line in adif_siv.read_siv_payload (line 33)
critical_code_review_comments: ingest_relayed_payload: no upper bound on data_time (future-date lockout, described above)

A snapshot with 0 arrivals but newer data_time replaces _last (alerts and arrivals) but leaves the arrival cache alone. GET then reports source='siv' with alerts and cancelled count from that snapshot, mixed with arrivals from an older snapshot. Edge case only.

Adif data_time has 7 fractional digits ('...57.3736507Z'). Python 3.11 fromisoformat and Chrome parse it. If an older Safari returns NaN in new Date(), staleSivStations treats the copy as fresh (NaN > x is false), so that device never relays. Harmless, but parsing the string more strictly would be more robust.

success_rate.backend: 100% (8/8 relay tests + 6/6 existing SIV tests, 1 skip)
success_rate.frontend: 100% (relay POST, alerts UI, source text, fresh-copy no-POST, partial stale, historical no-relay, auto-recovery)

seed_data_creation: test_duplicate_rejected posts one fake Atocha snapshot (no trains, data_time = now-5s). It was replaced automatically by a real browser relay about 4 minutes later. The current state holds real Adif data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use RN Web tabs: the 'Calle' dropdown, then 'Trenes'. Log in with 'Soy taxista', placeholder inputs 'Nombre de usuario'/'Contraseña' and data-testid=login-button. The time range is under Ajustes > 'Ahora' > 'HH:00 - HH:00' options. Creating files in /app/backend triggers uvicorn hot-reload, which wipes the in-memory SIV state (_last). The relay only fires when the server copy is older than 4 min or source!='siv'.
